_README: Machine 002 settings. Every number and rule the scripts use lives here. Rulings are dated and attributed to Chris. Edit here, not in the scripts.

cluster.market: Organizations that own and run a recurring event for an adult early-childhood workforce audience — ALL org types in ONE bucket, no order by type (ruling 2026-10-20)
cluster.next_markets_queue: After ECE is exhausted: HR / L&D departments, learning organizations, for-purpose organizations' conferences (ruling 2026-10-13). Each needs its own Green Sheet first.

waves._rule: Chris 2026-10-20: work by time, not by state or org type. Estimate each event's 2027 month (confirmed date if posted, else same month as the last dated edition). Reach out ~6 months ahead. Start with Jan–May 2027 events now for a busy spring. No events in 2026; anything in 2027 is fair game, including October 2027.
waves.wave1_order: soonest event first (default — Jan–Apr events get less than 6 months' notice)

qualification_gates._rule: Gates the DRAFTER applies before an event gets an Email 1. The refresh only records the facts.
qualification_gates.keynote_path_required: Chris 2026-10-19 (NAA27): conferences whose open call is breakouts-only with no external keynote path are not targets. Events with keynote_slot 'no' are not drafted; 'unknown' is drafted only after a human look.
qualification_gates.hold_if_keynote_announced: If the next edition's keynote is already announced, hold until the following cycle (design 2026-10-13).
qualification_gates.rfp_goes_to_bid_lane: procurement 'rfp' → bid lane, not cold email (design 2026-10-13).
qualification_gates.do_not_contact: Anyone on ../do-not-contact/register.jsonl is never contacted by any machine (ruling 2026-10-13, permanent).

refresh._rule: Chris 2026-10-20: every refresh (button or schedule) does the same four things — find new events, re-check every listed event's website for a confirmed 2027 date, fill gaps (person in charge, date, website), and flag any open call for proposals / presenters / RFP.
refresh.trigger: Scheduled task 'Conference event refresh (Machine 002)' with NO schedule — start it with Run now, or ask Claude in chat to refresh the event list. A schedule can be added later without changing anything else.
refresh.research_model: sonnet (one research agent per segment, run in parallel)
never: write a date without a source URL

search_budget._rule: Learned 2026-10-22: one run (one turn) gets 200 WebSearch calls TOTAL, shared by every agent. Re-checks use WebFetch on the known event_url (no search cost); searches go to finding new events and filling gaps.

refresh._2026_10_23: Chris 2026-10-23: build the full list now (one big run), confirm events now rather than nightly, present for review; Stage 3 (people + Apollo) only on his say-so. Target 2,000 organizations by end of May 2027 at 25 Email 1s per sending day. Head Start grantee universe from the OHS dataset: Lists/conference-pipeline/head-start-grantees/.

drafting.status: LIVE 2026-10-23 — copy file Marketing/Cold-Outreach-Sequence-Conference.md (E1 v2, E2 v1, E3 v1). Round 0: 9 Email 1 drafts created by Zapier 2026-10-23 (see runs/2026-10-23/round0-drafts.jsonl). Nightly drafter + follow-up sender not yet built; follow-ups for Round 0 are due 2026-10-30 (E2) and 2026-11-06 (E3).
open_rulings: Orgs Machine 001 emailed that never replied (silent no-reply): never re-contact, re-contact after N months with the conference offer, or Email 4 on the old thread?
Two-clusters-in-test cap: does 002 displace CL-2026-Q4 ELC Directors, or does CL-2026-Q3 CCR&R close?
Nightly drafter time (must not overlap 001's 3 AM MT run).
Colorado events: 001 reserves Colorado for Chris personally — same for 002?
Events with no past date found: hold on a 'date unknown' list, or Email 1 asks them when their event is?

labels._note: Mirror Machine 001's set; /2 /3 ★ X ⚠ ⏸ to be created when the follow-up sender is built

email_1_attachment._why: Chris's own template send to <ASSISTANT_EMAIL> 2026-10-23; fetch a fresh hydrate reference every run

zapier.gif: HST_WorkshopInAction.gif stays manual — Chris drops it in after the results bullets (Zapier cannot embed inline)
zapier.html_rules: one tag per line (newline between tags) so Zapier's text/plain part keeps the bullets on separate lines

vertical_of_org_type._rule: Chris 2026-10-23: adjacent verticals go in the same list, tagged so patterns can be analysed later. ECE = early-childhood workforce buyers; adjacent = school systems, for-purpose and HR/L&D associations.

machine_001_exclusion._rule: Chris 2026-10-23: the ~411 organizations Machine 001 has emailed are EXCLUDED from Machine 002 for now. Computed field excluded_machine_001 = true when the event/org domain matches Machine 001's contacted.jsonl. Rows stay in the database; the drafter never drafts them. Snapshot of the domains: exclusions-machine1-domains-2026-10-23.txt

evidence_grade._rule: Computed per event by bin/events.py: A = a named outside keynote (keynote_slot yes) or a documented RFP; B = an annual event with a confirmed or estimated 2027 date; C = organization or event recorded, event date/keynote unverified. Chris 2026-10-23: tag rows so the funnel can be cut by segment, vertical and evidence later.

geography._rule: Chris 2026-10-23: CO, KY and GA — off-limits in Machine 001 — are FAIR GAME for Machine 002. Any event/org that could be connected to an existing client (HubSpot customer, open deal, or a Clients/ folder org) is HELD and flagged for Chris to review a warm-intro path before any cold email.

recipients._rule: Chris 2026-10-23: Machine 001's thread rule applies — 1 in To, up to 2 in Cc, three people never four; the greeting names every first name on the thread; the Cc is insurance (one bounce still leaves two people who can hold each other to replying). Tiers are re-cut for the conference buyer.
recipients.to: The person who OWNS the event: conference chair, Director of Events/Conferences/Professional Learning, or the ED when the ED runs it
recipients.cc1: The budget-holder — ED / CEO / President / Superintendent / Head of School / Dean — when not already the To
recipients.cc2: The second person the org's own pages tie to the event: program/events coordinator, conference committee chair, PD director, division director over the event
recipients.selection_pool: Everyone named on the EVENT page + the staff/leadership page. The event page outranks the staff page because it names who actually runs the event.
recipients.checks: Every address passes Check 1 (named on the org's own pages) and Check 2 (Apollo/validator). Tier-1/2 people with no published address are looked up before the thread is built (never choose three from a pool of one — CAPA-2026-08-18). Generic inboxes are tier 4, never an exclusion. Never guess a pronoun.
recipients.bounce: Email 2/3 carry Machine 001's bounce parenthetical when a recipient from Email 1 hard-bounced: '(I think I got <First>'s email address wrong, so I'm not including them on this)' — its own line under the greeting.
